      - heading "Understand Interior Angles on the Same Side" [level=2]
  - text: CLASS 9 · EUCLIDEAN GEOMETRY
  - heading "Interior Angles on the Same Side" [level=1]
  - paragraph: Explore co-interior (same-side interior) angles and their supplementary relationship.
  - text: ◷ 30 min RIGOROUS geometry2d
  - navigation:
    - button "⚗ Interact"
    - button "▣ Learn"
    - button "▱ Example"
    - button "◫ Formula"
    - button "⌘ Practice"
  - main:
    - heading "TRANSVERSAL INTERACTIVE" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Select the same-side interior angle pair and explore.
    - button "Parallel Lines"
    - button "Nonparallel Lines"
    - article:
      - img "Interactive same-side interior diagram": ∠1 ∠2 l m t
      - complementary:
        - text: ⌁ C-pattern (Same-side interior)
        - paragraph: ∠1 and ∠2 are co-interior angles.
    - complementary:
      - heading "1. SELECT ANGLE PAIR" [level=3]
      - button "∠1 & ∠2 same-side interior ✓"
      - button "∠3 & ∠4 same-side interior"
      - heading "2. MEASURE ANGLES" [level=3]
      - text: ∠1 =
      - strong: 62°
      - button "−"
      - button "+"
      - text: ∠2 =
      - strong: 118°
      - button "−"
      - button "+"
      - heading "3. SUM (SUPPLEMENTARY CHECK)" [level=3]
      - strong:
        - text: 62° + 118° = 180°
        - img
      - slider "Angle sum": "180"
      - text: Balanced! Sum is 180°. ☝ Drag the purple transversal or use ± to change one angle. The other updates.
    - img
    - text: Great! For parallel lines, same-side interior angles are supplementary. Their sum is 180°.
    - article:
      - heading "💡 WHY IT WORKS" [level=2]
      - paragraph: When two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, the interior angles on the same side lie on a straight line when one line is slid over the other without rotation.
      - paragraph: Hence, they are supplementary.
      - strong: Straight line ⟶ 180°
      - text: ∠1 + ∠2 = 180°
    - article:
      - heading "▣ WORKED EXAMPLE" [level=2]
      - paragraph: If one same-side interior angle is 73°, what is the other?
      - paragraph: Given ∠1 = 73°
      - paragraph: Since ∠1 + ∠2 = 180°
      - paragraph: So ∠2 = 180° − 73° = 107°
      - text: "Answer: ∠2 = 107°"
    - article:
      - heading "♙ KEY FACT (THEOREM)" [level=2]
      - paragraph: For parallel lines cut by a transversal, same-side interior angles are supplementary.
      - text: ∠1 + ∠2 = 180°
      - paragraph: "Converse: If a pair of same-side interior angles are supplementary, then the lines are parallel."
    - article:
      - heading "△ COMMON MISCONCEPTION" [level=2]
      - paragraph: Same-side interior angles are supplementary, not generally equal.
      - figure:
        - text: Not Equal (in general)
        - img: 62° 118°
        - text: ×
      - figure:
        - text: Supplementary (correct)
        - img: 62° 118°
        - text: ✓
      - text: They add to 180°, but are not usually equal.
    - article:
      - 'heading "◎ CHALLENGE: MAKE THEM 180°" [level=2]'
      - paragraph: Rotate line m until the selected same-side interior angles add to 180°. Then verify parallelism.
      - img "Interactive same-side interior diagram": ∠1 ∠2 l m t 62° 118°
      - text: Rotate line m
      - slider "Rotate line m": "14"
      - text: 14°
      - button "Reset":
        - img
        - text: Reset
      - button "Check Parallelism"
      - img
      - text: Perfect! ∠1 + ∠2 = 180°. Lines l and m are parallel.
